newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals cautions S.Africans on investing overseas.
newsitem.headline: Stals cautions S.Africans on investing overseas.

text.p: South Africa's Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals on Monday welcomed a recent easing of foreign exchange controls, but cautioned South Africans, wary of the economic situation at home, from rushing to invest overseas.
In his maiden budget last week Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced a package of reforms that will help free up South African individuals and corporates to invest cash outside the country.
Stals said in a speech to a businessmen in Durban that the move opened up new vistas of opportunity for South Africa.
"The removal of exchange controls opens up new opportunities for South African corporates, institutional investors and private individuals," he said.
But Stals warned that the fickle and risky world of international finance could just as soon burn investors' fingers as reward them with riches.
"(All investors) must give careful consideration before any decision is taken to invest hard earned savings in a foreign country, in a foreign currency and in a foreign institution," he said.
Stals said the risk factor was particularly applicable to private investors.

"Very few private individuals in South Africa have the knowledge and the expertise to manage foreign investment portfolios and to assess the alien risk exposures that are connected to such investments," he said.
Stals said investing abroad held new and volatile risks for South Africans who may be encouraged to invest overseas after 1996's dramatic fall in the rand.

But the once-ailing currency has stabilised recently and Stals said an investor who had put money from rand into sterling when the exchange rate had hit eight rand to the pound, would now have made a serious loss as the level is currently nearer seven rand.

"Foreign investments will, however, hold new risk exposures for South African investors, particularly in an environment of volatile international exchange rates. The timing of the transfer of an investment into a foreign currency can be detrimental," he said.
